title: Emery insists Garnacho can turn Villa fortunes around
subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutEmery insists Garnacho can turn Villa fortunes aroundShareAlejandro Garnacho failed to make Aston Villa's squad against Galatasaray, following a difficult start to his loan spell.Unai Emery insists Alejandro Garnacho can turn things around at Aston Villa, despite a difficult start to his loan tenure.
The Argentine joined Villa on a season-long loan from Chelsea, with the Villans reportedly having an obligation to buy him if he reaches a certain number of appearances.
Garnacho has struggled so far under Emery, failing to score or assist in seven matches this season, with all of his appearances coming off the bench.

Among players to have made at least seven appearances across Europe's top five leagues this season, only Charly Alcaraz (Everton) and Carlos Espi (Real Madrid) have played fewer minutes than Garnacho (95).
Garnacho was left out of the Villa squad for their trip to Galatasaray in midweek, with Emery instead choosing two goalkeepers and only filling 11 of his 12 substitute spots.
However, the Spaniard has encouraged Garnacho to keep improving and pushing for a place in the squad.
"When he is not involved in the squad, it is because I have to choose from other players as well," Emery said.
"He has my respect first as a person and second as a player, but he is not involved for this reason.
"But football can change. We are playing matches so I will need players.
"Alejandro Garnacho is training very well. His attitude is fantastic, a very good attitude.
"He was struggling at the beginning of the season because he was not fit. Now he is fit and he's training at a good level.
"So keep going, keep moving forward as a club, as a team, he himself as a player, and we will see it."
Villa, who are winless in their last six games across all competitions (D3 L3), face Ipswich Town in the Premier League on Saturday.
